messages:

Cc: Theo Ramos <theo@cloudedge.io>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial topology & request: validate lattice mapping for on-prem cutover

Hi Camila,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Attached is the rough ‘lattice’ topology our infra team sketched for the private deploy into our primary colo. We want Redwood to validate two things before the July 18 cutover window:

1) Control plane reachability from the VPC control plane proxy (NAT + TLS boundary).
2) Data plane egress rules and mandatory hop-through points for auditing.
3) Failover expectations if the primary egress path to Redwood Dedicated is congested.

We’re also curious whether a small TCP multiplexer at the edge (to consolidate outbound sockets) will break your service discovery or KV cache warmup expectations.

Attaching diagram: vpc-lattice-diagram-v1.png (PNG, 1.6MB).

Can your team review by Thu EOD and flag anything that would block the cutover? Happy to set a 30m call if that helps.

—Samantha
Samantha Lee

Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 11:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial topology & request: validate lattice mapping for on-prem cutover

Samantha — thanks for the diagram and the clear checklist. We reviewed quickly with infra and here are the initial observations:

- Control plane: overall shape looks fine. We need an explicit TLS termination boundary for control RPCs (we recommend the control-proxy terminate + mTLS to Redwood control plane).
- Data plane: the multiplexor is acceptable provided it preserves source IP or injects an x-forwarded-for equivalent header that we can consume for audit logs. If the multiplexer rewrites source ports aggressively, it will complicate our KV cache affinity during warmup.
- Egress failover: we can support a primary + secondary egress route. We’ll need a small routing policy on the control plane side to prefer the lower-latency path and fallback if health checks fail.

I’ve attached a draft cutover checklist and annotated the diagram with two suggested guard rails. Please review and confirm the multiplexor behavior (socket rewrite vs header preservation).

Proposed next steps:
- ACME: confirm multiplexor behavior by Thu 06/01 EOD (Samantha)
- Redwood infra: produce a hardened controlplane tls termination guide (Jonas) by Fri 07/02
- Ops runbook: add egress failover test case to cutover checklist (Irene) by Fri 07/02

I can host a 30m call Thu 06/01 10:00-10:30 PT or 14:00-14:30 PT. Which works?

Camila Reyes
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial topology & request: validate lattice mapping for on-prem cutover

Quick technical review notes (high level):

- TLS termination: agree with mTLS between control-proxy and Redwood control plane. Ensure SNI is preserved so we can route to the correct tenant shard on inbound.
- Multiplexer: if it performs NAT30-style pooling (many internal -> few external IPs) we need a per-session 5-tuple mapping for token-based affinity to work; otherwise we should rely on our session cookie that travels in the TLS payload. 
- KV cache warmup: add a small pre-warm job during cutover that issues a sequence of canonical prompts to populate top-K caches; schedule it to run in the maintenance window.
- Health checks: we prefer an application-level health check (HTTP 200 + readiness header) over plain TCP for failover decisions.

Blocking items:
- We need ACME to confirm whether the multiplexer preserves SNI and/or adds x-forwarded-for. If neither is present, we will require a small NAT exemption so client-source preservation remains intact.

Jonas
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood-inference.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood-inference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood-inference.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood-inference.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha@acme-corp.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial topology & request: validate lattice mapping for on-prem cutover

Adding a couple of operational notes from an egress and security perspective:

- Audit hops: every outbound inference request needs a traceable hop-id. If the multiplexer collapses flows, insist that the multiplexer emit a hop-id that we can consume and persist in our audit trail.
- Rate-limiting: during the initial warmup we should advertise a slightly elevated token quota for the tenant for 2 hours to avoid throttling during cache priming. Camila — I can prepare an ephemeral quota plan if ACME agrees.
- Cert rotation: on the control plane TLS termination recommendation, include a cert rollover timeline and fallback certs in the runbook. We saw issues during a prior on-prem rotation when fallback certs were missing.

Rishi
Manager, Infrastructure Reliability, Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — good alignment. Samantha, I’ll summarize the immediate asks below so we have a single source of truth for the cutover runbook:

- Confirm multiplexor behavior: does it preserve SNI and/or inject x-forwarded-for? If it rewrites source IPs/ports, provide a configuration that exempts control-plane flows.
- Share any firewall rules that will be inbound to the control-proxy so we can validate iptables and TLS neighbors.

Redwood actions (owner in parentheses):
- Hardened TLS guide with SNI and cert-rotation steps (Jonas) — due Fri 07/02
- Add egress failover test case and audit hop-id ingestion to cutover checklist (Irene) — due Fri 07/02
- Temporary quota bump plan for warmup window (Rishi) — draft by Fri 07/02

I’ll schedule the 30m call for Thu 07/01 10:00 PT and send a calendar invite; please let me know if you prefer the afternoon slot. After ACME confirms multiplexor behavior we’ll finalize the cutover checklist and lock the maintenance window.
